terms.gloss: fail at no point, leave nothing undone
terms.grammar: dēsum with nūllō locō, “in no place, at no point”
evidence: Cic. Fam. 16.4: adhūc dum mihi nūllō locō deesse vīs, numquam tē cōnfirmāre potuistī (Lewis & Short), s.v. adhūc
terms.comment: Cicero to Tiro, who was so eager not to fail him in anything that he never got well. The dē- of deesse is short before the vowel.

terms.gloss: leave nothing undone, leave no stone unturned
evidence: Cic. Att. 9.2a.1: quam nihil praetermittis in cōnsiliō dandō! (Lewis & Short)

sources: Lewis & Short: desum · Lewis & Short: locus

phrases.english: I will leave no stone unturned.
